fact: The Central Bank of Liberia's Guidelines Concerning Digital Credit for Financial Institutions, taking effect 17 March 2022, set consumer-protection requirements (disclosure, prohibitions, complaint handling, data privacy, a US$400 loan cap) for banks, non-bank financial institutions and licensed mobile money entities offering digital credit, under Consumer Protection and Market Conduct Regulations No. CBL/RSD/004/2020.
system: Guidelines Concerning Digital Credit for Financial Institutions

fact: The Central Bank of Liberia issued Regulation CBL/RSD/004/2020 on consumer protection and market conduct on 8 January 2020, taking effect on Gazette publication, applying to all regulated financial institutions and including e-banking security duties and digital credit disclosure rules (credit up to US$33).
system: Regulations Concerning Consumer Protection and Market Conduct (CBL/RSD/004/2020)

fact: The regulation requires each financial institution to run a consumer help desk and lets a dissatisfied consumer escalate to the Consumer Protection Unit of the Central Bank of Liberia's Regulation and Supervision Department, which must respond within one month.
system: Consumer Protection Unit, Central Bank of Liberia
